glossary.Iron absorption: Uptake of dietary iron through the duodenum into the blood.
glossary.Pituitary: The gland under the brain that controls other glands, including the gonads.
glossary.Northern European ancestry: Family origins in northern Europe, where HFE mutations are most common.
glossary.Fatigue: Persistent tiredness not relieved by rest.
glossary.Diabetes mellitus: Raised blood glucose from lack of insulin or insulin resistance.
glossary.Large-joint arthropathy: Joint disease affecting big joints such as knees and hips.
glossary.Jaundice: Yellowing of skin and eyes from raised bilirubin, here from liver disease.
glossary.Erectile dysfunction: Inability to get or keep an erection.
glossary.Hepatocellular carcinoma: Primary liver cancer, a risk in cirrhosis.
glossary.Heart failure: The heart cannot pump enough blood for the body's needs.
glossary.Iron studies: Blood tests of iron status: serum iron, ferritin, transferrin and transferrin saturation.
glossary.Serum ferritin: Blood level of ferritin, the iron storage protein; also rises with inflammation.
glossary.Genetic testing: Testing DNA for a disease-causing variant, here HFE mutations.
glossary.Therapeutic phlebotomy: Removing blood on purpose to lower iron, the same as venesection.
glossary.Iron chelating agent: A drug that binds iron so it can be excreted.
glossary.Decompensated cirrhosis: Cirrhosis with failing liver function: ascites, jaundice, encephalopathy or variceal bleeding.
glossary.Vitamin C: Ascorbic acid; it boosts iron absorption from the gut.
glossary.Raw shellfish: Uncooked seafood that can carry Vibrio vulnificus, which thrives in iron overload.
glossary.Dermal: Relating to the dermis, the deeper layer of the skin.
glossary.Restrictive cardiomyopathy: Stiff heart muscle that cannot fill properly.
glossary.Dilated cardiomyopathy: Enlarged, weak heart chambers that pump poorly.
glossary.Mutation: A change in the DNA sequence of a gene.
glossary.Insulin secretion: Release of insulin from pancreatic beta cells.
